For your stir-fry, a good soy sauce substitute that maintains the savory, umami flavor profile is coconut aminos. It is made from the sap of coconut blossoms and salt, making it soy-free and gluten-free. It has a slightly sweeter and less salty taste than traditional soy sauce, so you may want to add a splash of vinegar or a pinch of salt to balance the flavor if needed. Another option is tamari if the person is only allergic to soy proteins but not gluten, but since the allergy is to soy, coconut aminos is the safer and more direct alternative.
